title: Scenario 13: ClearPass says ACCEPT, the switch says no
task: Admins should log in over SSH with their ClearPass accounts (TACACS at 192.0.2.10, key cppm-tac-key), with the switch's own admin account only when ClearPass is down. Set that up and log in as tac-admins with `sim ssh tac-admins`. ClearPass logs ACCEPT and the switch still says no: find out why and fix the profile in the ClearPass panel. Get tac-admins in as an administrator and tac-helpdesk in read-only. Then turn on command authorization for SSH through ClearPass, see what it does to the switch's own admin account, and take it back out.
hints: `tacacs-server host 192.0.2.10 key plaintext cppm-tac-key`, `aaa group server tacacs CPPM-TAC` with `server 192.0.2.10`, then `aaa authentication login ssh group CPPM-TAC local`.

`sim ssh tac-admins`: Permission denied, while the ClearPass panel shows ACCEPT. The profile sets only the Privilege Level in its header, and the switch needs a Shell attribute to know which group the user belongs in.

In the ClearPass panel give Lab-Admins Shell priv-lvl 15 or Aruba-Admin-Role administrators, and Lab-Helpdesk Shell priv-lvl 1 or Aruba-Admin-Role operators. When a profile sends both, Aruba-Admin-Role wins.

Stay in the terminal you started in: it is the switch's own admin, logged in over SSH before any of this. `aaa authorization commands ssh group CPPM-TAC none` asks y/n first, and after it that session can't run even `show clock`, because ClearPass doesn't know admin. `sim ssh tac-admins` (or `sim console`), then `no aaa authorization commands ssh`.

`sim ssh admin` is refused once TACACS answers: ClearPass rejects admin as unknown and, without allow-fail-through, the switch never tries the local password. That is the safe setting. The console is the way in when you need the local account.

checks.desc: The TACACS server is configured with its key
SSH logins try a TACACS group first and local after it
tac-admins logs in as an administrator
Command authorization is back out, so the local admin can work again
No allow-fail-through: a ClearPass reject is a no, not a try at the local password
